reason: An API sends a streaming chat as chat.accept/v1 only when the project's current owner declares it; a cold project (no owner after a Core start or idle retirement) gets http.invoke/v1, whose streamed response the owner serves for the whole turn while the project's ordered work lane waits (renames/archives/other sends waited up to 17 minutes under host pressure). The kernel now publishes its typed chat transports and the owner's DurableHttpRunner renames a claimed http.invoke chat start to chat.accept/v1 or chat.resume/v1 under its fence (new RuntimeCoordination.retype_chat_start) before invoking it. Review fixes: chat_binding reads the binding before the command (no final-looking 409 across a rename), and a failed rename keeps the HTTP transport instead of going uncertain. Selected: chat acceptance (new tests incl. Postgres variants), delivery, coordination, execution worker, acceptance compatibility and API worker suites.
exclusions: test_runtime_chat_stream.py also exercises the journal, but 5 of its SQLite cases fail identically on pristine origin/main and with this patch, so it is not selected; test_runtime_chat_resume.py's SQLite cases already fail at the merge base (viewer helper ValueError) and are not selected. Process-level suites (test_execution_worker_process.py) need a pidfd-capable interpreter and are not run. No UI, native or Playwright cases: no frontend code changed. Real-Core evidence (scratch Postgres Core, cold project, with and without the host-pressure queue at default thresholds) is recorded in the PR, not executed by CI.
